paragraphs: Here's the big idea, friend: God finishes what He starts, and He does it with people who are still being worked on. Moses had a burning bush, a clear order and the staff of God in his hand, and he STILL had a rough stretch on the road. The LORD told him plainly that He would harden Pharaoh's heart, so Moses walked in knowing this would not be quick (Exodus 4:21). That tells me God never hid the hard part from him, and He doesn't hide it from you either.

Now look at the lodging place, because it's heavy. The LORD met Moses and was about to kill him, and it was Zipporah who acted, and then the LORD let him alone (Exodus 4:24-26). I think this tells us that when God gives an assignment, the way we walk into it matters to Him. Being called doesn't mean being careless, and being chosen doesn't mean being excused.

Then look at who God sends to meet Moses. Aaron shows up and kisses his brother, and together they gather the elders (Exodus 4:27-29). The people hear that the LORD had attended to the Israelites and had seen their affliction, and they bow down and worship (Exodus 4:31). So when you feel like nobody sees what you're going through, remember that God does, and He sends help to you too. Keep the oven warm, baker, because this story is NOT over.
